noticias.titulo: ¿Por qué acrygel uñas es la solución ideal para uñas débiles?
noticias.texto:
¿Por qué acrygel uñas es la solución ideal para uñas débiles?
¿Por qué acrygel uñas es la solución ideal para uñas débiles?
Las uñas débiles y quebradizas son uno de los problemas más comunes entre los clientes de la industria nail. El contacto constante con agua, los productos químicos domésticos e incluso el estrés pueden empeorar su estado. En estos casos, el esmalte tradicional a menudo no ofrece el resultado deseado. Por eso, cada vez más profesionales y clientes eligen acrygel uñas como una solución eficaz que combina fortalecimiento y estética.
Qué es acrygel uñas y cómo funciona
Acrygel uñas es un híbrido moderno de dos materiales: gel y acrílico. Combina las mejores propiedades de ambos: la resistencia del acrílico y la flexibilidad del gel. Gracias a su textura plástica, el material se modela fácilmente, permitiendo crear una forma natural de la uña sin volumen excesivo.
Su principal ventaja es su capacidad para fortalecer la placa ungueal sin sobrecargarla. Esto es especialmente importante para clientes con uñas finas y debilitadas.
Problemas principales de las uñas débiles
Para entender por qué acrygel uñas funciona, es importante prestar atención a los problemas típicos:
- Fragilidad y tendencia a astillarse incluso con mínima presión
- Deslaminación, que afecta no solo la apariencia sino también la estructura de la uña
- Excesiva finura, que hace que las uñas sean vulnerables
- Crecimiento lento, que impide alcanzar la longitud deseada
En estas condiciones, la manicura deja de ser solo estética. Las uñas necesitan una protección pensada, delicada pero eficaz, que no solo oculte el problema, sino que cree un entorno para su recuperación gradual.
¿Por qué el gel acrílico es la mejor opción?
Su versatilidad y fórmula pensada han convertido a este material en el favorito tanto de profesionales como de clientes que esperan un resultado perfecto sin compromisos.
- Fortalecimiento sin sobrecarga
El acrígel es mucho más ligero que el acrílico clásico, pero al mismo tiempo proporciona una base sólida. No crea sensación de “uñas pesadas” ni ejerce presión sobre la uña natural.
- Protección contra la fragilidad
El material forma una estructura resistente que protege las uñas de daños mecánicos. Gracias a esto, se reduce significativamente el riesgo de grietas y astilladuras.
- Apariencia natural
El acrígel permite crear un recubrimiento fino y cuidado, que se ve lo más natural posible. Es la opción ideal para quienes valoran la elegancia y el minimalismo.
- Comodidad al usarlo
A diferencia de muchos otros materiales, el acrígel casi no provoca molestias durante la polimerización. Su flexibilidad también ayuda a evitar lesiones en la uña.
En resumen, el acrígel no es solo una alternativa a otros materiales, sino una solución pensada que combina funcionalidad y estética, ofreciendo un resultado duradero y seguro.
Quién se beneficia especialmente del acrígel
Este material es la elección óptima para:
- Personas con uñas crónicamente débiles
- Clientes después de retirar extensiones
- Quienes tienen esmalte de gel que se descascarilla rápidamente
- Quienes desean dejar crecer la longitud natural de las uñas
Por eso, en los salones se recomienda a menudo el acrígel como solución básica para la recuperación de uñas.
Cuidado de las uñas con acrígel
Para mantener el resultado perfecto, es importante seguir algunas reglas simples:
- Hacer correcciones cada 2–3 semanas
- Usar aceite para cutículas regularmente
- Evitar cargas mecánicas fuertes
Este enfoque permite no solo conservar la estética de la manicura, sino también mejorar gradualmente el estado de las uñas naturales.
Conclusión
El acrígel no es solo una tendencia, sino una solución pensada para quienes enfrentan el problema de uñas débiles. Combina resistencia, comodidad y apariencia natural, ofreciendo un resultado duradero. Si buscas una manera de fortalecer tus uñas y al mismo tiempo lograr una manicura impecable, el acrígel es la elección óptima.

noticias.titulo: A lo concreto: ecotasa turística Por José Cabrera Noda
noticias.texto:
A lo concreto: ecotasa turística Por José Cabrera Noda
Secretario de Política Municipal, Sector Primario, Alimentación y Soberanía Alimentaria PSOE de Fuerteventura
Defiendo la implantación de una ecotasa turística como herramienta de financiación para la conservación ambiental y la mejora de la calidad de vida en Fuerteventura con criterios de sostenibilidad y concreción. No es un eslogan: es un planteamiento político concreto. Tan concreto como decir que debemos darle una solución permanente a la carretera entre Morro Jable y La Punta de Jandía. Veamos si ambos planteamientos concretos pueden confluir.
La ecotasa turística que defiendo para Fuerteventura no es una medida recaudatoria genérica, sino un instrumento finalista. Se recaudaría para financiar acciones concretas. No estoy inventando la pólvora, pero sí metiendo el dedo en un asunto que escuece a algunos sectores económicos de la isla. La ecotasa turística (que se aplica al visitante, no al residente) es un concepto ampliamente aplicado, conocido y aceptado en todo tipo de destinos europeos, por lo que el argumento de que como reacción vendrían menos turistas a la isla, afectando al empleo y la economía local, se desmonta por sí mismo.
El reto es hacer un uso inteligente de la medida y no implantarla por imitación de otros destinos. Si la futura ecotasa turística de Fuerteventura se dedica a acciones concretas de conservación ambiental y mejora de la calidad de vida de las personas que vivimos en la isla, bienvenida sea.
El ejemplo que se me viene a la cabeza es la carretera de La Punta de Jandía. Aquí hay un problema que debemos abordar con una solución estratégica y permanente. El sistema del recebe ya no es una solución. Cada vez es más complicado encontrar el material fino para igualar, rellenar los huecos y consolidar el firme de los 23 kilómetros de esta carretera. Y sacar ese árido del entorno de Jandía no parece lo más adecuado ni lo más sostenible desde los puntos de vista ambiental y paisajístico.
Ahí está el dilema que planteo para una de las vías más definitorias del ser majorero, de nuestra esencia, y también de nuestra imagen exterior. El sistema del recebe está alcanzando su final operativo y, con ello, mermará la seguridad en el tránsito de vehículos. Eso será otro problema añadido que se traducirá en accidentes de tráfico. Así que debemos encontrar otra solución y, en mi opinión, debe ser una solución permanente.
Para hacer realidad esa futura solución permanente para la carretera de La Punta de Jandía se necesita la confluencia de dos cosas: una solución técnica y jurídica que supere la actual etapa del tren de recebe y financiación para llevarla a término.
Para el primer condicionante se deberá congeniar el tránsito seguro de vehículos con las normas del Parque Natural de Jandía… otros muchos parques naturales tienen carreteras a las que se les ha dado una solución permanente. El segundo condicionante puede resolverse con una decisión política valiente y de largo recorrido: crear una ecotasa turística en Fuerteventura, de
naturaleza finalista, donde los majoreros y majoreras podamos decidir dónde invertir, en concreto, ese dinero. Para nuestro bienestar, para conservar nuestros paisajes, para empoderarnos en nuestro territorio. Una ecotasa turística para mejorar en lo concreto.

noticias.titulo: El viento llegará a Fuerteventura sobre las 5 de la mañana
noticias.texto:
El viento llegará a Fuerteventura sobre las 5 de la mañana
Todo apunta a un pico de intensidad a las 14.00 horas
La jornada de este miércoles será muy ventosa en toda la isla de Fuerteventura, con aviso naranja de la Aemet en la isla y alerta por vientos en todo el archipiélago. La isla de La Palma está en aviso rojo.
Todo apunta a que el viento comenzará a soplar a partir de las 5 de la mañana, pero será a las 7 cuando alcance bastante intensidad en toda la isla, especialmente al norte y noroeste.
Si quieren recibir esta y toda la información GRATIS de Fuerteventura y Canarias puntualmente a través de nuestro canal de whatsApp, que no es un chat y no se puede enviar ni recibir comentarios, solamente información y videos de la isla, apuntarse al canal de Noticias Fuerteventura.
El pico de viento del suroeste se espera a las 14.00 horas con rachas que podrían superar los 90 kilómetros por hora. Se recomienda mucha precaución con elementos ornamentales árboles y sobre todo en zonas costeras, donde además se pueden medir olas de hasta tres metros de altura.
Según todas las previsiones la fuerza del viento comenzará a amainar a partir de las 6 de la tarde, que será cuando Charles nos rebase rumbo a la península ibérica.

noticias.titulo: Puerto del Rosario recibe la primera visita del impresionante crucero Mein Schiff Relax
noticias.texto:
Puerto del Rosario recibe la primera visita del impresionante crucero Mein Schiff Relax
Dispone de 14 restaurantes y 17 bares, amplia zona de spa con 6 tipos de saunas gratuitas, terraza al aire libre y piscinas con vistas panorámicas
 Redacción NoticiasFuerteventura
Llega por primera vez a Puerto del Rosario el Crucero Mein Schiff Relax, un crucero de primer nivel mundial propulsado por gas licuado y referente en la navegación planetaria.
En la mañana de este jueves el alcalde, David de Vera, la concejala de Turismo, Rosa Rodríguez, la representación de la Autoridad Portuaria y la empresa consignataria, daban la bienvenida al crucero y fueron recibidos por el capitán Todd Burgmann y su equipo.
Por parte del ayuntamiento se obsequió al capitán con una cesta de productos típicos de la isla : queso, aceite, licor de leche de cabra, aloe vera, etc junto a algunas publicaciones del ayuntamiento, incluyendo el libreto de la exposición "The Canarian". El capitán hacía entrega de la tradicional metopa de esta nueva embarcación.
El Mein Schiff Relax es el primer crucero de la nueva clase "InTUItion" de la naviera alemana TUI Cruises, inaugurado en 2025.
Características principales:
* Tamaño y capacidad:
Mide aproximadamente 333 metros de eslora, cuenta con 19 cubiertas y puede albergar hasta 3.984 pasajeros y cerca de 1.400 tripulantes.
* Oferta gastronómica y de ocio:
Dispone de 14 restaurantes y 17 bares, una amplia zona de bienestar (spa) con 6 tipos de saunas gratuitas, terraza al aire libre, piscinas con vistas panorámicas y la Infinity Pool en la proa. Gimnasio 24 h. Pabellón cubierto y auditorio para 800 personas con actuaciones en directo, entre otros servicios.
* Sostenibilidad:
Funciona con un sistema de propulsión de gas natural licuado (GNL/LNG) y tecnologías avanzadas de eficiencia energética
En las encuestas de la propia empresa resaltan que en este destino aumenta la satisfacción de los clientes y el número de actividades que realizan en el exterior.

noticias.titulo: Elba inaugura su megaresort de Corralejo
noticias.texto:
Elba inaugura su megaresort de Corralejo
Elba Corralejo Resort & Spa, con capacidad para 1.000 plazas, recibía a los primeros huéspedes el 1 pasado de noviembre
Hoteles Elba ha inaugurado oficialmente su megaresort de Fuerteventura, el Elba Corralejo Resort & Spa, el más grande de la isla con 478 habitaciones y una capacidad de 1.000 plazas, y el séptimo de la cadena en este destino, tras dos años de obras y una inversión de 100 millones de euros.
"Con Elba Corralejo reiteramos nuestra sólida vocación de permanencia en Canarias, generando empleo y enriqueciendo la oferta turística con una propuesta de valor diferenciada y experiencias memorables", señaló Ángel Jove González, presidente de Anjoca, propietario de la cadena.
Miguel Ángel Rodríguez, en representación de Turismo del Gobierno de Canarias destacó que el Hotel Elba Corralejo "representa el modelo de calidad por el que apuesta Canarias, al tratarse de un establecimiento de cuatro estrellas que ha acreditado el cumplimiento de los criterios de excelencia y ecoeficiencia exigidos por la normativa turística".

noticias.titulo: El Majorero Gabri tendrá su primera titularidad en Segunda División con el CD Tenerife
noticias.texto:
El Majorero Gabri tendrá su primera titularidad en Segunda División con el CD Tenerife
El guardameta majorero ocupará la portería del CD Tenerife ante el Ceuta por la sanción de Dani Martín y debutará como titular en la categoría
El guardameta majorero Gabri De Vuyst tendrá una oportunidad especial este domingo al estrenarse como titular en Segunda División con el CD Tenerife. El futbolista, nacido en Fuerteventura en 2004, ocupará la portería blanquiazul frente al Ceuta, en el encuentro que se disputará a las 12:00 horas en el Heliodoro Rodríguez López.
Su presencia en el once llega como consecuencia de la sanción de Dani Martín, expulsado en los últimos minutos del partido frente al Andorra. El portero asturiano vio dos tarjetas en el tramo final del encuentro, la segunda por lanzar el balón contra un adversario.
Para Gabri será su novena participación con el primer equipo del Tenerife. Hasta ahora ha disputado cinco encuentros en Primera RFEF, dos en la Copa del Rey y los últimos minutos del choque ante el Andorra, en el que encajó el gol del empate.
El majorero afronta así su primera gran oportunidad en el fútbol profesional. Su balance hasta el momento es de tres victorias, dos empates y tres derrotas, con seis goles encajados y cuatro partidos con la portería a cero.

noticias.titulo: El verano acompañará todo noviembre en Fuerteventura
noticias.texto:
El verano acompañará todo noviembre en Fuerteventura
Vientos flojos del este, y temperaturas sobre los 25 grados, nos acompañan durante todo el mes
 Redacción NoticiasFuerteventura
El otoño sigue siendo verano en la isla de Fuerteventura, al menos en cuanto a las temperaturas. Tras el paso de varias borrascas atlánticas que no han dejado grandes acumulados en la isla, todos los modelos apuntan a una segunda quincena de noviembre con tiempo anticiclónico y temperaturas veraniegas.
Vientos flojos de nor-noreste, cielos despejados la mayor parte del día y el mercurio por encima de 25 grados en muchas zonas del interior y del sur serán la tónica, al menos hasta fin de mes.
Si quieren recibir esta y toda la información GRATIS de Fuerteventura y Canarias puntualmente a través de nuestro canal de whatsApp, que no es un chat y no se puede enviar ni recibir comentarios, solamente información y videos de la isla, apuntarse al canal de Noticias Fuerteventura.
Todos los modelos apuntan a que tendremos un mes de noviembre más cálido de lo normal, en un año que está resultando especialmente cálido por el fenómeno climático El Niño, que está modulando todo el clima planetario.
Aguas más calientes en todo el litoral majorero y con el mar en relativa calma, olas que pueden llegar a 1.5 metros pero que subirán con fuerza a partir del miércoles de esta semana entrante. Se recomienda precaución en el baño en toda Fuerteventura, pero especialmente al norte y oeste de la isla.

noticias.titulo: How the attack on Crimean Bridge unfolded
noticias.resumen: One of the key symbols of Russia's occupation of Ukraine has suffered major damage after a seven-stage attack by Kyiv.
noticias.texto:
How the attack on Putin's prized Crimean Bridge unfolded
- Published
Stretching across the Kerch Strait in the Black Sea, the Crimean Bridge was always a symbol: for Russia, a prestige project cementing its claim to sovereign Ukrainian territory, and for Ukraine, a hated piece of infrastructure emblematic of Moscow's occupation of the Crimean Peninsula.
A key section of the double-arched, 12-mile-long bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said that the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".
But eight years after its unveiling, the bridge has now become material proof of Kyiv's ability to pierce through Moscow's military defences to hit even its most treasured and protected structures.
How did the seven-stage operation play out?
The attack on the strategic Crimean Bridge was carried out gradually to cut across several layers of defence, Kyiv confirmed on Tuesday.
For several weeks Ukraine's Security Service and its General Staff gradually destroyed air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets, and other designated targets, President Volodymyr Zelensky said.
A significant strike had already been reported on 16 November, when drones hit the bridge at night. Traffic was paused briefly then reinstated, and although the arch over the road section was visibly damaged, the structure remained standing.
But that hit turned out to have been only the penultimate stage of a complex attack.
In the early hours of 17 November, the final strikes dealt a fatal blow to the weakened arch structure.
One verified video - filmed from a camera on board a Ukrainian-made Flamingo missile - shows the weapon approaching the main span of the bridge and heading towards the steel arches, with the footage freezing just before impact.
The Flamingo had potentially been modified to be controlled remotely, which improved its accuracy enough to strike the bridge supports, munitions expert Justin Bronk, from the Royal United Services Institute said.
The missile's "very heavy warhead" made it "more suitable" for attacking the bridge's reinforced concrete spans and supports, Bronk added.
Zelensky later confirmed that several types of missiles and drones had been employed in the attack, which led the massive road arch - weighing thousands of tonnes and measuring about 227m in length - to collapse into the strait.
Daylight images taken from the shores of Crimea to the north show a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was too dragged below into the sea.
This is clearly critical damage to the crossing. Far from just being a decorative feature of the bridge, the arch played a structural role, transferring loads and supporting the span and helping to ensure the stability of the entire structure.
The parallel arch supporting the railway section has remained standing, although it may also have been damaged. All traffic on the bridge was initially suspended, though trains were later allowed to resume running.
But the damage to the bridge's main span is "catastrophic", Colin Capriani, a structural engineer from Monash University in Melbourne, Australia, told BBC Verify. It was "very hard to envisage" how the bridge could be rebuilt given it is clearly well within range of Ukrainian weaponry, Capriani added.
Major attacks in 2022 and 2023 had already caused serious damage to the road spans of the bridge, but the structure survived.
The difference this time is "the most critical and vulnerable part of the bridge has been hit", said David MacKenzie of engineering consultancy COWI, adding that "although the wreckage of the bridge can be cleared fairly quickly, reinstating full road traffic will take over a year".
What effect could the collapse of the bridge have on Crimea?
Moscow uses Crimea as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles. From there it also carries out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplies its troops in southern Ukraine.
The attack comes after a summer of frequent strikes on Crimea, dictated by Ukraine's stated goal of cutting the peninsula off from Russia. At the time, Kyiv vowed to turn the Crimean Peninsula "into an island".
Now - although it is too early to speak of a complete blockade of Crimea â the risk of a serious transport and logistics crisis has increased significantly.
There is still a land corridor running through the occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions. However, Ukraine has been systematically striking transport routes across northern Crimea, as well as bridges and other crossings in the area around Chongar, which has already caused problems with the delivery of fuel and other supplies, including military cargo.
Moscow can also still utilise the ferry crossing across the Kerch Strait. It could partly compensate for the loss of the bridge, but its capacity is very limited - and anything on the Black Sea has become vulnerable to attack. Resupplying Crimea by sea is risky, as Ukrainian naval and aerial drones operate extensively in the area.
In addition, debris from the Crimean Bridge - particularly its enormous arch - may have blocked the shipping channel. This would make it harder for larger vessels to pass through and create further problems for ports in the Sea of Azov, including the occupied cities of Mariupol and Berdyansk.
Away from the operational value of the damage to the bridge, the symbolic significance remains.
In 2018, Putin triumphantly drove over the bridge representing the unification of Russia and Crimea in a Russian-made truck. That section of the road now lays on the seabed.
Nearly five years since he launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Putin continues to wreak destruction on Ukraine's civilian population, but his most prized symbols of power are increasingly threatened by Kyiv's reach.

noticias.titulo: Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss
noticias.resumen: Huang says he has had an "outpouring" of calls from investors and others calling for him to return.
noticias.texto:
Jensen Huang pushes Nvidia comeback after board rejects pressure to reinstate ex-boss
- Published
Jensen Huang said he would be "honoured" to return as the boss of tech giant Nvidia if the board asked him to, in his first public comments since his shock resignation.
"I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely," Huang said on X, days after reports he had extramarital affairs, including with an alleged Chinese spy.
He said he had an "outpouring" of calls from company employees, investors and others calling for him to return as CEO of Nvidia.
But, as the BBC reported on Monday, Nvidia's board is not considering bringing him back to lead the company.
The prospect of Huang returning at this point looks unlikely.
The company's board is investigating his conduct, which includes an alleged affair with an Nvidia executive.
The AI chip giant is set to report its financial results later on Tuesday, during which the company's interim chief executive, Collette Kress, may address the situation with Huang.
Beyond the internal Nvidia investigation, Huang's affair with a woman suspected of being an asset for Beijing is set to see the billionaire questioned before multiple committees of US lawmakers in the weeks ahead.
The Nvidia founder said he had "made serious mistakes in my personal life".
Nonetheless, Huang's statement appeared to show some hope he would be able to move past the major corporate scandal.
Huang said people have continued to "reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics".
"If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO," Huang added.
Many technology executives in recent days have praised Huang's role in the artificial intelligence boom. A petition began circulating online over the weekend calling for his reinstatement at the company.
Yet, by Monday, many executives were not openly calling for Huang's return.
Brad Gerstner, a major tech investor who knows Huang personally and also holds a significant stake in Nvidia, last week wrote an open letter saying that Nvidia could consider Huang's reinstatement.
On Monday, Gerstner said during an event hosted by Semafor that his letter had been misunderstood and the investigation into Huang's conduct needed to run its course.
While Gerstner questioned the facts around Huang's departure, he added: "I don't know to what degree he misled the board. If I was on a board I would take that very seriously. Let's be clear no one is above the law."

noticias.titulo: Trump lands in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
noticias.resumen: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".
noticias.texto:
Trump lands in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
- Published
President Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.
A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel.
Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with America's partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese.
"Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said.
"We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added.
Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Donald Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components.
The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China.
But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines.
After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would".

noticias.titulo: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
noticias.resumen: States have reported over 5,400 cases and 10 measles-related deaths for the first time since the early 1990s.
noticias.texto:
US loses measles elimination status after 26 years amid record case numbers
- Published
After more than two decades, the US has lost its measles-free status, following two years of record case numbers and deaths.
The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), a specialised service of the United Nations, determined the US has had uninterrupted transmission of the same strain of measles for more than 12 months.
Dr Jarbas Barbosa, director of PAHO, announced that Mexico and Bolivia have also lost their measles elimination status, attributing the resurgence in the region to persistent "gaps in vaccination".
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said it was committed to "regaining measles elimination status" by expanding access to vaccines.
The US has seen 5,400 cases of measles this year alone, with 10 measles-related deaths, the most the country has seen since the 1990s.
The measles virus - with its signature blotchy red rash - used to infect millions of children a year before a vaccine was invented. The extremely contagious virus can be fatal, and some patients can experience long-term complications including encephalitis and immune amnesia, which resets the immune system, leaving it with only limited ability to respond to new infections.
The US recommends two measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shots for children between ages one and six, which is 97% effective in protecting against the illness.
PAHO, a group within the World Health Organization, revoked the US's measles-elimination after determining that the virus had circulated nonstop for more than a year.
"These figures are a serious warning for our region," PAHO's director Barbosa said at a news conference on Tuesday. "Measles is resurging globally amid persistent gaps in vaccination."
He added that Canada, which lost its status of having eliminated measles last year after seeing several large outbreaks, has made strides this year to interrupt transmission.
Daniel Salas, the executive manager of immunisations at PAHO, said that the US and others who lost elimination status would be required to submit corrective action plans outlining how they would attempt to improve vaccination rates.
US Health Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr Kennedy has attempted to make a series of sweeping changes to US vaccine recommendations and policies. The vaccine sceptic has also frequently cast doubt on the safety of MMR shot, as vaccination rates have declined across the US in recent years.
Kennedy has argued that the rise in measles cases started before he took the helm at HHS and that neighbouring countries have also seen more infections.
Responding to Tuesday's announcement, the CDC said the agency and its partners were "committed to stopping measles outbreaks, protecting Americans, and regaining measles elimination status".
"Together, we will encourage MMR vaccination, expand access to vaccines, and help communities close gaps in protection," the agency said.
CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the measles elimination designation was not what protected Americans.
"Vaccination does," she said. "We know where transmission is occurring and we've invested $100 million in state and local health departments to reach those communities."
The UK, Spain and Austria were among European nations that lost their measles-free status earlier this year, along with countries including Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.
Nuwan Gunawardhana, an assistant professor of medicine with Columbia University Irving Medical Center, said the US losing its elimination status was "a huge leap backwards".
The US was the first country to eliminate measles in the Americas thanks to vaccination campaigns, noted William Moss, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.
Dr Gunawardhana said it took massive efforts from public health officials and clinicians to build trust with patients to increase uptake of the MMR vaccine, leading to decades in the US with few infections and deaths.
But that trust has been steadily eroding since the Covid-19 pandemic, when Dr Gunawardhana said patients were confronted with misinformation about the safety of vaccines and lost even more trust in public health systems.
The vaccination rate for MMR across the US has fallen to 92.4%, below the 95% level that provides herd immunity, which limits the spread of measles and protects those who cannot get vaccinated, including newborns.
An outbreak in Pennsylvania has infected over 1,400 people - likely a large underestimate - and killed seven people, according to state officials.
Kennedy, the health secretary, has sparred with Pennsylvania officials over how it is counting the measles deaths, with CDC declining for now to record some of the deaths in its database.
Last year, the health secretary fired all the members of a top vaccine advisory panel and replaced them with his own appointees, some of whom were vaccine critics.
The panel recommended a number of vaccine changes - including no longer requiring the Hepatitis B vaccine for all newborns - but those recommendations were blocked by a federal judge.
President Donald Trump this year also cast doubt on the safety of the MMR vaccine, issuing an executive order for the shot to be split into three separate immunisations for measles, mumps and rubella, a move public health experts say is costly and could sow confusion about an already safe vaccine.
Doctors and public health officials say the misinformation from Kennedy and Trump has played a major role in falling vaccination rates.
"It's confusing patients. It's confusing families," Dr Gunawardhana said. "We need a clear message from the top."
The federal government's vaccine manoeuvres have left public health officials and states to fill in the gaps, offering their own separate recommendations upholding decades-long practices.

  - Published30 January
  - Published24 September

noticias.titulo: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
noticias.resumen: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.
noticias.texto:
Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
- Published
A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.
There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.
According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response. It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.
There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.
They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.
All settlements are illegal under international law.
Local Palestinians said that the events in al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Monday night began with harassment by Israeli settlers. Children threw stones, they said, and the settlers opened fire, killing Fadda al-Fahidat, who was 72, outside her home.
According to Palestinian accounts, her son rushed to the scene in his car after hearing the news and collided with an empty Israeli settler car parked outside his family home, injuring settlers who were standing nearby. The settlers then fired more shots, they said.
The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle".
Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat."
The IDF said that Israeli security forces were sent to the scene and were pursuing suspects.
Doctors at a hospital in Jericho said that al-Fahidat was shot in the head. Several other Palestinians and Israelis were injured, reports said.
The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement.
Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents.
In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent.
The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident.
Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now.
It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank".
The UK government said on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable.

noticias.titulo: 'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
noticias.resumen: Moscow has targeted bridges in Kyiv, while Ukraine severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.
noticias.texto:
'It was really scary': Mother describes sheltering during Russia strikes on Kyiv bridge
- Published
The alarms warning of a ballistic missile threat went off just before 23:30 on Monday in Kyiv. Moments later came the boom of explosions.
Once again, the main bridges over the broad River Dnipro that cuts through the city were the target and this time the Russian missiles hit what they wanted.
Close to one end of the Pivnichnyi (Northern) bridge there is a large crater and in the pouring rain, water now rushes through it to the river below. Chunks of tarmac and metal are scattered around.
At its broadest point, the jagged hole is about eight metres wide.
The crossing is closed to all traffic apart from the occasional fire engine or police car passing at high speed. By contrast, nearby roads are jammed with cars and trucks, forced to take long detours.
Anyone in a hurry to move around this city has to walk, or cycle, across the bridge, picking their way through the wreckage. In the miserable weather, that also means getting very wet.
Masha and her family moved to a flat next to the bridge because they had been living by a power plant that kept getting hit by Russian missiles.
Last night, she was in the kitchen of their new place when the Russians struck the bridge. She thought her windows would be blown out of their frames by the explosions.
"It was really scary. We had no idea they'd hit here so much. It's like we're cursed," Masha told me, describing grabbing her child and running into the corridor for protection.
But somehow, she still managed to sound cheerful.
"It's difficult, but we're used to it. And we try to take the positive from everything. Like: we survived today! So we can be happy about that."
From the damage, it looks like Russia targeted the same spot on the bridge with a volley of three missiles, aiming to keep the road closed for as long as possible.
A major recovery operation is under way, with firefighters and engineers in fluorescent overalls working to evaluate the extent of the damage. But it looks like the disruption will continue for some time.
Further along the Dnipro River, the Pivdennyi (Southern) bridge was also hit on Monday night, with four missiles.
The metro line across it was suspended for a while, although by mid-afternoon it had been restored. The mayor, Vitali Klitschko, said road transport in one direction was also being partially restored.
On the Pivnichnyi bridge, a man with a bag of tennis rackets on his back was gazing at the crater in front of him. He was heading home from the courts after he had travelled on foot to the left bank.
"It is upsetting," Anatolii told us. "Then when you read the news of what our side did to the Crimea bridge, you do feel a bit better."
That is because there was a battle of the bridges overnight.
Ukrainian missiles hit the one Russia had built to occupied Crimea, and caused serious damage. That bridge is prized by Russian President Vladimir Putin personally, a symbol of his illegal 2014 takeover.
Ukrainians loathe it for the same reason and now a section has collapsed into the sea, along with its towering arch.
To many here, the timing feels significant: a blow to Putin's image, just as he wants to seem most powerful at this week's summit with the US and China.
But for Kyiv resident Antonina, today is just another challenge to overcome.
The 67-year-old, who we met pulling a shopping trolley through the debris on a bridge in the Ukrainian capital, was heading to see her son on the right bank, but taxi drivers were charging a fortune to go round, so she decided to walk.
"What else could I do?" she shrugged.
"It was a very scary night. It felt like something exploded right over my head. We will get through this, but I just wish the war would end."

noticias.titulo: Indian woman gang-raped while pregnant in 2002 'heartbroken' after two perpetrators bailed
noticias.resumen: Bilkis Bano has spoken of her "pain, shock and disbelief" at the top court order and vowed to fight back.
noticias.texto:
Gujarat riots gang-rape survivor 'heartbroken' after bail for two convicts
- Published
The article has details that some readers may find disturbing
A pregnant Muslim woman who was gang-raped and saw 14 family members murdered during the 2002 Gujarat riots has spoken of her "pain, shock and disbelief" after two of her rapists were recently granted bail.
Bilkis Bano said in a statement that she heard about the top court order through press reports and vowed to fight back.
The freed men are from a group of 11 convicts - part of a Hindu mob - serving life terms for the attack on Bano.
All the men were also freed in 2022 after a Gujarat government order. That decision, and the celebrations as they left prison, caused global outrage. In 2024, the Supreme Court overturned the order.
In a short three-page order dated 28 October, the Supreme Court granted bail to Bipinchand Kanaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya and suspended their sentences while their petition challenging a 2017 Bombay High Court order is being heard.
The judges explained that the early release was because the two convicts "have been under incarceration for a period of more than 17 years" and "that one of the appellants has a severe handicap".
On Tuesday, Bano's lawyer Shobha Gupta told the BBC that the news of Joshi and Modhiya's release had left "Bilkis heartbroken".
"She has to restart her battle for justice. She had no information that this case was coming up in the Supreme Court. What is troubling for us is that every time something like this happens, we worry that it could affect her faith in judiciary."
Gupta said it was difficult to understand why the convicts were being released because "it's not a routine criminal case, it's a case that shocks the conscience of the world, of entire humanity".
The attack on Bano and her family was one of the most horrific crimes during the Gujarat riots, which began after 60 Hindu pilgrims were killed in a fire on a passenger train in the town of Godhra.
Hindu mobs attacked Muslim neighbourhoods, blaming them for starting the fire. The riots continued for three days and more than 1,000 people died, most of them Muslims.
When rioters attacked Bano's village and started setting Muslim homes on fire, she and 16 relatives went on the run. She was 19, had a three-year-old daughter and was pregnant with her second child.
They were attacked on the morning of 3 March 2002 by a group of men "with swords and sticks", she told me in 2017. Her three-year-old daughter, she said, was snatched from her lap and killed.
Her attackers were her neighbours, men she had seen almost daily while growing up. They tore off her clothes and several of them raped her, ignoring her pleas for mercy.
Her cousin, who had given birth two days earlier, was raped and murdered and her newborn baby was killed too.
Bano survived only because she lost consciousness and her attackers left, believing she was dead. Two boys - seven and four - were the only other survivors of the massacre.
Her fight for justice has been long and nightmarish. The first arrests were made only in 2004 after the Supreme Court called in federal investigators and transferred her case to Mumbai, saying that courts in Gujarat could not deliver justice to her.
In her statement released on Monday night, Bano spoke of "fresh tears of pain, shock and disbelief".
"I still cannot believe that once again, for the second time, an order has been passed by the Supreme Court without calling me up and without hearing me," she said.
"For 24 long years, I have stood up to fight for justice... again and again. Yet today, I find myself losing the very justice I had fought so hard to win.... And I am scared of losing faith in justice, yet again."
Bano vowed to "fight this order... for my children, who do not deserve to live haunted by fears and scars for the rest of their lives".
"I do this for my three-year-old Saleha who deserved to live and whose memory demands justice. I do this for women everywhere. Because no woman, no survivor, no citizen should have to endure this eternal test of belonging and equality, and fight for justice for the rest of her life."
Prime Minister Narendra Modi was Gujarat chief minister at the time of the riots, and was criticised for not doing enough to prevent the carnage. He has always denied wrongdoing and has not apologised for the riots.
In 2013, a Supreme Court panel also said that there was insufficient evidence to prosecute him. But critics have continued to blame him for the riots happening on his watch.

noticias.titulo: Nvidia partner Megaspeed being investigated by US government over chip exports
noticias.resumen: The Singapore-based company is suspected of helping to ship high-end AI chips from tech giant Nvidia to China, violating US export rules.
noticias.texto:
US government confirms investigation into tech firm Megaspeed
- Published
The United States has confirmed it is investigating computing company Megaspeed, suspecting it of violating US export controls by helping to ship tech giant Nvidia's chips to China.
In a joint statement, the US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce said they had been investigating Singapore-based firm Megaspeed since 2024.
It comes after questions were raised about the possibility high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
Concerns emerged in recent weeks after Nvidia founder Jensen Huang revealed he had an extramarital affair, allegedly with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. US authorities suspect her of spying for Beijing, which China denies.
Jensen Huang resigned from his role as chief executive last week following revelations he had two affairs.
Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and is suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.
The justice and commerce departments said on Monday that "it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information" regarding the investigation.
Laying out a timeline, it said it began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".
In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia "concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed". In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list.
Agents from the Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, then conducted an on-site check at Megaspeed that month and interviewed Alice Huang, who was chief executive at the time.
Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.
The Nvidia scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end chips to Megaspeed.
On Friday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the US Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for failing to properly oversee the export of the chips.
Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.
The White House said on Monday it would further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia.
The reported affairs by Jensen Huang created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a major company in the AI industry and central to the US as it competes with China for dominance.
In the statement, the US government said it would "bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred".
They added: "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the US economy, and the Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce will remain vigilant in pursuing justice for those who want to compromise America's technological edge."

noticias.titulo: Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
noticias.resumen: Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as "baseless".
noticias.texto:
Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
- Published
President Donald Trump has said the US is taking "very seriously" the potential for any Iranian plot to attack Washington DC, after he was asked about a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments.
In the Philippines, where he attended the Asean Summit, Trump nodded when asked by a journalist about the report that Tehran was planning to detonate a so-called dirty bomb in the US capital and said: "We're looking into it."
CNN cited unnamed US intelligence officials suggesting Iran could target senior figures in Trump's administration with such an attack.
Iran called the claim "baseless." Concerns about dirty bombs grew after the 9/11 attacks in 2001, although no such attack has ever occurred.
Such a device would contain radioactive material - such as uranium - which would be scattered through the air when its conventional explosive detonated.
The BBC has not independently verified CNN's reporting.
During his comments to reporters in Manila, Trump was asked whether there was reason to believe an attack was imminent.
"I hope it's not," he said, "but we take it very seriously because they [the Iranians] happen to be crazy."
In a statement before Trump's comments, White House spokesperson Lauren Bis wrote: "We remain vigilant monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland."
Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rebutted the CNN article and other US reports.
He posted on X: "Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations."
Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran's parliamentary speaker and chief negotiator in indirect talks with the US, was similarly dismissive of the CNN report.
"Same false flags, same war mongering, new logos," he posted on X.
Mick Mulroy, a former CIA paramilitary officer and deputy assistant defence secretary, told the BBC: "A dirty bomb is not difficult to make or deploy."
"Although it is not a weapon of mass destruction, it can be a weapon of mass disruption," he added.
Imran Bayoumi, a geostrategy expert with the Atlantic Council in Washington DC and former policy adviser to the defence department, said that it remains "unclear how serious" would be the threat of a supposed Iranian dirty bomb.
"But Iran has planned and threatened to attack the US in the past," he said. "It is also unclear why this report is becoming public now."
It comes as intelligence officials and members of the Trump administration seek congressional renewal of a key national security law.
Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (Fisa), which allows the US to âspy on foreign nationals, expires next March.

noticias.titulo: UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
noticias.resumen: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
noticias.texto:
UK sanctions firms over Israeli West Bank settlements
- Published
The UK has sanctioned companies it said are involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.
The construction of settlements, which are illegal under international law, has risen sharply in recent years. Settler attacks on Palestinians and their property have also surged.
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar called the sanctions a "hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies".
Criticising the move on X, he wrote that Israel - as it has done in the past - will respond with "countermeasures", and that "decisions will be announced in due course".
"Israel will not bow to external pressure or change its policies as a result," Saar said, adding that they will "consider new ways to strengthen Jewish communities" in the West Bank, and "protect those involved in developing and building".
Israel previously condemned UK sanctions related to West Bank settlements, accusing the Labour government of "systematically acting against the State of Israel".
The Palestinian foreign ministry welcomed the sanctions and called on other countries to follow suit.
It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the highly sensitive E1 area east of Jerusalem.
The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and cut it off from East Jerusalem.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine".
The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza.
Responding to the announcement, the group said: "Tzav 9 is a movement of abiding citizens from all the political spectrum, and we've always protested peacefully."
It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world.
The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements and the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK.
Miliband said: "Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach.
"That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution.
"The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.
"We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike."
'New approach'
In September, the UK government announced that it would ban the import of goods from Israeli settlements, as well as acting against companies and individuals providing services for settlement expansion.
At the time, Miliband said the move marked the beginning of a "new approach" to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, which "not only calls out injustice and suffering, but acts".
That announcement prompted a furious reaction from Israel, which said it would shut the British consulate in East Jerusalem in retaliation.
Last month, most diplomats left the consulate - which handled UK relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem as well as in the West Bank and Gaza - but the UK insisted that the building would not be closing and would operate as a "UK mission".
Israel has built about 160 settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them.
There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

noticias.titulo: Carney eyes 'other options' for embattled Canadian auto sector on China trip
noticias.resumen: The PM has suggested Chinese automakers could replace American ones in Canada - but some say that would not be easy.
noticias.texto:
Carney eyes 'other options' for embattled Canadian auto sector on China trip
- Published
The plight of Canada's car industry has become one of the clearest stress tests of Ottawa's effort to weather US tariffs and chart a path forward.
The past year and a half has been tough on the sector since US President Donald Trump imposed a 25% tariff on non-American-made vehicles, upending decades of free trade and automotive integration with Canada.
Now Prime Minister Mark Carney has signalled that he is looking to China, where he is on a visit for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit (Apec), as part of the solution.
But that avenue is not without controversy, and is once again drawing the ire of those close to Trump.
While in Cambodia earlier this week, Carney told reporters that Canada could turn to European and Asian carmakers to save its auto manufacturing sector if a trade deal with the US could not be reached.
"Look - great auto workers, important market, real assets in Canada," he said. "If they're not fully utilised in a North American context, that provides other opportunities.
"Canada's going to move forward either way."
He went on to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in China on Tuesday for their second head-to-head in less than a year. The two talked afterwards of the importance of developing their relations, and Carney said they had agreed to further tariff cuts.
Neither side mentioned vehicles specifically, though analysts suggest the issue will have been prominent in their minds.
In January, Carney said that opening the door to China's electric vehicles, external (EV) could result in investment into Canadian-owned companies and the creation of manufacturing jobs in the sector.
American tariffs on imports of Canadian-made vehicles have led to thousands of job losses in Canada and anxiety over the future, as 90% of cars made in Canada are shipped to and sold in the US.
At the same time, China has been eyeing Canada as a potential entry-point to the North American EV market. Earlier this year, Canada announced that it would let in 49,000 EVs from China at a low tariff rate, with plans to raise that quota gradually to 70,000 by 2030.
The move was a significant break from the US, which has tariffed Chinese EVs heavily since the presidency of Joe Biden to protect domestic manufacturing.
Chinese EV manufacturers like BYD and Chery have already been lobbying the Canadian government for access.
Last week, Canada's Minister of International Trade Maninder Sidhu toured a Chery plant in China, external to discuss their potential entry to the Canadian market. He told reporters afterwards that Canadians could expect to see affordable Chinese electric vehicles for sale in Canada by early 2027.
These moves come as the toll of US tariffs on Canada's auto sector has become harder to ignore.
Stellantis, a multinational car manufacturer that made models like the Dodge Challenger and the Chrysler 300 in Canada, recently announced it would sell its assembly plant in Brampton, Ontario - a move that Carney characterised as a "betrayal" of the plant's 2,200 workers.
The facility had been idle since 2023 for a planned retooling, but what was supposed to be a temporary shutdown became permanent after Trump's tariffs, leading the company to shift some manufacturing to Illinois in the US.
Stellantis said it would sell part of its Brampton plant to Roshel, a Canadian defence contractor and manufacturer of armoured vehicles.
The Canadian auto workers' union has expressed concern about the deal, calling it "underhanded" and warned that Canada would lose thousands of high-paying jobs as a result.
The deal has also led to speculation that a Chinese EV manufacturer could move into the facility, after Canadian media outlet CTV News reported, external, citing anonymous sources, that Stellantis was planning to lease back 25% of its plant to assemble "affordable" EVs.
- Canada's deal with China signals it is serious about shift from US 
  - Published16 January
- How China made electric vehicles mainstream 
  - Published23 June 2025
There are prominent voices who oppose any such move, including within Canadian politics.
In a letter to Carney, Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned against opening the door for Chinese EV kits to be assembled in Canada at the Brampton plant.
China overwhelmingly builds its cars at home and ships them whole - or to be assembled in kits - overseas.
Lynette Ong, director of the China Governance Lab at the University of Toronto, said introducing Chinese auto manufacturing in Canada would be "controversial" due to fears that Canadian jobs could be lost and that the North American auto manufacturing industry could be eroded.
"We want to make sure they're hiring Canadian workers, that they are helping train Canadian workers and that they are transferring the technology over," Ong said.
She argued that Canada should also be wary of making itself vulnerable to potential security breaches and foreign interference from China, as well as risking the ire of the Trump administration.
That already appears to be happening. Peter Navarro, Trump's senior counsel for trade and manufacturing, warned Carney against cosying up to China in a post on X, external.
"Are u really threatening to play China off the U.S.? This is offensive in the extreme," he wrote on Monday. "You should be far more worried China is going to eat Canada alive."
His comments were reposted by Pete Hoekstra, the US ambassador to Canada.
Canadians' views of China have grown more positive since Trump's return to the White House. An Angus Reid poll released on Tuesday, external suggests many are open to Chinese investment in the EV sector, but with additional security or restrictions.
The Carney government has set terms for China's entry to Canada's auto market, including that any venture should be jointly-owned by a Canadian company, that it must follow Canadian labour standards and that the cars should be built using Canadian-made parts.
Ahead of his meeting with Xi on Tuesday, Carney also noted there are "clear guardrails" in how Canada deals with China, including barring work on sensitive matters like artificial intelligence and critical minerals.
Canada has also eyed other partnerships. It is notably pursuing associate member status with the EU, and had signed a free trade deal with the Philippines earlier this week.
Just how much Canada is willing to embrace Chinese manufacturing, however, still depends on the outcome of ongoing US-Canada trade talks.
Progress has been made in negotiations with the US, Carney recently said, but differences remain. It is unclear if Trump and Carney will speak on the sidelines of the Apec summit later this week.

noticias.titulo: Gunmen kill Costa Rican journalist who reported on drugs trade
noticias.resumen: Rodríguez had denounced alleged links between criminal organisations and powerful figures in Costa Rica.
noticias.texto:
Gunmen kill Costa Rican journalist who reported on drugs trade
- Published
A Costa Rican journalist who denounced alleged links between politicians and drug traffickers in the Central American country has been shot dead.
Police said gunmen on a motorbike ambushed Camilo RodrÃguez, 50, as he was travelling in his car north of the capital, San JosÃ©, on Monday afternoon.
The independent reporter earlier said he had been receiving death threats from drug trafficking gangs.
Local media reported that it was the first murder of a journalist in more than two decades in Costa Rica. It comes at a time when transnational crime gangs are increasing their presence in the country, driving up its formerly low homicide rate.
The president of the Costa Rican Journalists' Association, Yanancy Noguera, said that "all evidence so far points to the silencing of a dissenting voice in Costa Rica - a person who published information about organised crime in the country".
RodrÃguez had been working as a journalist for several decades, both in radio and in print.
Most recently, he had been uploading videos to social media in which he named public figures such as judges, business people and politicians, which he alleged were corrupt or had ties to known drug traffickers.
In one of his videos, he alleged that the home of Costa Rica's President, Laura FernÃ¡ndez, had been constructed by a company that he said had links to a criminal gang.
FernÃ¡ndez, who categorically denied any wrongdoing, took the journalist to court, accusing him of defamation.
Reacting to his murder in a video message, the president strongly condemned the attack, calling it "a stain on freedom of expression".
She added that she had instructed police to do their utmost to "punish Camilo's murderers".
RodrÃguez had also tried to stand for political office, seeking to run as the presidential candidate for the Costa Rican Renovation Party in 2021.
However, his candidacy was rejected by the electoral authorities after the party failed to meet the necessary criteria required to file candidates.
Costa Rica's Attorney General, Carlo DÃaz, said that "silencing someone who reports on drug trafficking or corruption, in this case a communicator, is a signal we cannot tolerate in a democratic society".

noticias.titulo: How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China
noticias.resumen: The new rules restrict chip exports and also access to their computing power, which China relies on heavily.
noticias.texto:
How new US chip restrictions on South East Asia will hit China
- Published
As US President Donald Trump heads to China, his administration has renewed efforts to curb Beijing's access to advanced semiconductors.
On Monday, Washington announced new interim rules that will increase scrutiny of data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
The move not only restricts the export of advanced chips, but also access to their computing power, which Chinese firms currently rent abroad to train artificial intelligence (AI) models.
South East Asian countries in particular have invested heavily in data centres to power their AI ambitions - and Chinese firms seeking computing power overseas have been a key market.
But now these firms will need a US government licence to buy advanced chips from Nvidia or other American chipmakers. This allows Washington to monitor if those chips are being used to serve Chinese companies, or being smuggled to China.
This poses a fresh challenge for Beijing, which has become deeply dependent on compute from abroad in the wake of US export restrictions. At least 30% of China's advanced AI computing power is projected to come from renting overseas or smuggling in 2027, according to research by the Institute for Progress, external, a US-based think-tank.
China's foreign ministry called the new rules "economic coercion" and said Beijing "will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests".
A blow to Asia's AI boom
This is also a problem for South East Asian economies where large numbers of data centres have sprung up recently. Some of the firms behind them are accused of helping China evade US export controls on advanced chips.
One of those is Singaporean data centre firm Megaspeed, whose former director Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Calls for tighter export controls have grown after Nvidia's Jensen Huang admited to an affair with her and resigned as CEO.
Megaspeed, the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia, is accused of illegally smuggling chips to Chinese companies after purchasing them for use in data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
The company has denied these allegations, defended its business as "legitimate and lawful", and said it has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation". It also said Alice Huang stepped down from her role as director in late 2023 and left the firm last year.
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, however, has said Brazil and the four South East Asian nations "present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips that Washington wants to keep out of China's hands.
The new measures are aimed at ensuring sensitive US technology "cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the bureau added. Licences will be issued on a "case-by-case basis", it said.
Countries like Malaysia and Thailand whose data centre roll out has been heavily driven by Chinese buyers could be hit hardest, says international trade expert Naoise McDonagh from Australia's Edith Cowan University.
But the new rules are unlikely to derail the data centre boom as a whole, says Reema Bhattacharya from advisory firm Verisk Maplecroft, adding that investment backed by major tech firms and clearly identifiable customers should "remain relatively resilient".
Singapore was an early adopter of data centres but when it began limiting new construction, investment flowed to neighbours Malaysia and Thailand. Johor in Malaysia and Batam in Indonesia have also approved billions of dollars worth of data centres to catch the spillover demand.
These countries have been offering incentives such as cheaper land to attract foreign investment, including from Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent.
But now, the region could find it harder to get hold of advanced chips.
The BBC has contacted Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand for comment.
Singapore said it is "engaging relevant US authorities" to understand the new rules better, and is "exploring how to facilitate trusted access" for local firms.
A spokesperson for Brazil's Ministry of Development, Industry, Trade and Services said it is aware of the US announcement and it "is closely monitoring any potential developments regarding this measure".
Malaysia previously said it welcomes data centre investment but "will not allow itself to be used to get around export controls".
A headache for China
The new rules also come just ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week.
Beijing has made self-sufficiency in tech a national priority and needs the best chips to build powerful AI models.
Chinese firms DeepSeek and MoonShot have come close to US rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI. So much so that The Institute for Progress estimates top US AI models lead the best Chinese platforms by only about six and half months.
"This is despite US AI companies having significantly better compute access and financing," it said.
Still, China needs advanced US chips to ensure its best AI models are competitive, experts tell the BBC.
The new restrictions on South East Asia and Brazil have taken away "one of the more practical routes Chinese AI developers had to accessing frontier computing power," Bhattacharya said.
But tighter restrictions could also push Chinese firms towards domestic semiconductors and further drive advancement at home.
That has been a longstanding dilemma for Washington, McDonagh said: whether to keep selling chips to China to retain its reliance on the US, or restrict access and risk further spurring Chinese innovation.

noticias.titulo: Pretending to be in New Zealand, booking leave and buying consoles - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6
noticias.resumen: Sensor Tower estimates the game has already made $1.18bn from pre-orders across PlayStation and Xbox
noticias.texto:
Pretending to be in New Zealand, booking leave and buying consoles - the lengths fans are going to for GTA 6
- Published
Grand Theft Auto fans have waited 13 long years for the latest edition of the game to be released - and going to extreme lengths to be ready for its launch.
GTA 6 will be released at midnight on Thursday - and Victoria Evans, from West Sussex, is not leaving anything to chance.
She has her alarm set for 05:00 GMT, and has a day off booked. She says she put the game's release on her leave request form which was approved, she told BBC News, despite the fact her boss "doesn't know what GTA 6 is".
She's far from the only one. For the game's launch day, HR software company BrightHR, external looked at absence data from more than 1.2 million employees from 70,000 businesses across the UK.
It found GTA was mentioned in 4.6% of time-off requests by employees. Throughout November and December, it said an estimated 83,000 days had been booked off for the game.
And booking leave is only one of the ways fans are making sure for the big day. Others are buying a new console to play it on or even pretending they're halfway around the world to get early access.
Big demand
Market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates, external GTA 6 has already generated $1.18bn (Â£894m) from 12 million pre-orders - although Rockstar has not confirmed this.
Despite the option to preload the 212GB game, Jennifer Holmes, chief executive of the London Internet Exchange, said several UK internet providers including BT and Virgin Media had "increased capacity in anticipation of higher demand" ahead of launch.
- GTA 6 - all you need to know about Rockstar's blockbuster game 
  - Published15 October
Gamers have long been known to book time off work for major releases.
When Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in October 2018, social media users were sharing plans to take the day off, with one analytics firm reportedly finding, external more people talking about calling in sick for it than any other game that year.
Similar conversations took place ahead of Cyberpunk 2077's release in December 2020, with fans discussing, external taking several days off to play.
Some places have decided to lean into the trend for GTA 6 by offering incentives around the game - including the US Army's 3rd Infantry Division based at Fort Stewart, Georgia.
It gave some active-duty soldiers a four-day pass to play the game when it is released in November, as long as they sign a reenlistment contract for a minimum of two years between 1 August and 12 November.
"The idea was to have a unique incentives programme that connects to what soldiers are interested in," public affairs officer for the division, Lieutenant Colonel Angel Tomko confirmed to the BBC in August.
"There are 130 soldiers eligible within the battalion, and 20 have selected this incentive as part of their reenlistment," she said at the time.
Allow Instagram content?
This article contains content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. You may want to read Metaâs Instagram cookie policy, external and privacy policy, external before accepting. To view this content choose âaccept and continueâ.
Moving to New Zealand
Aside from taking time off, some gamers have also been discussing a technical loophole which could give them valuable extra hours of play before it officially unlocks in their country.
Because GTA 6 will release at midnight local time in all regions, New Zealand will become one of the first places where it is available, due to it reaching midnight earliest because of its position near the international date line.
This has led to some investigating ways to "trick" their consoles into thinking they're based in the island country when they are in fact thousands of miles away.
According to Google Trends, searches for the "GTA 6 New Zealand trick" have surged by more than 5,000% in the UK over the past month.
Games journalist Vic Hood said many gamers would be looking to play earlier to "get in on the action as soon as possible", as well as to prevent spoilers.
"As New Zealand is 13 hours ahead of the UK, that's 13 hours of gameplay that has time to spread across the internet and potentially spoil some key story beats and in-game surprises," she said.
"Took an extra day of paid time off when I found this out," one fan posted on Reddit on the trick.
It also means gamers would be playing the game at the much nicer time of 11:00 GMT, rather than having to stay up all night.
But another Xbox user shared caution on Reddit, noting that while the loophole had been exploited for many years for other game releases, GTA 6 "might be the game where Microsoft finally does something about this 'exploit'" - which could include banning players.
GTA 6's developers Rockstar and publishers Take Two Interactive have not commented on the loophole, and neither have Sony nor Microsoft.
Louise Wooldridge from Ampere Analysis said both Microsoft and Sony had "rules governing regional accounts and purchases" for the Xbox and PlayStation, adding that Sony's were "slightly more restrictive".
Players who choose to use the workaround could therefore risk breaching those terms and conditions and potentially face restrictions on their accounts or lose access to their digital games.
Some gamers will have to wait even longer than their console-playing counterparts to get their hands on GTA 6, as the game will not be available on PC at launch, similar to previous GTA releases.
"Spare a thought for the PC users who will have to live vicariously through others' YouTube videos and Twitch streams," gamer Stephen Finn told the BBC.
A PS5 now costs from Â£520, while the more powerful PS5 Pro is nearly Â£790.
Despite the hefty price tag, for some the temptation to join the community in playing what many have called the biggest game launch of the year, if not decade, has been too great.
Reddit posts and videos, such as one by US YouTuber isoish, external, show fans buying consoles specifically to play the game.
"So, the only game I'm going to have on here is GTA," the content creator said in the video.
"The whole PS5 is for GTA 6."
After more than a decade of waiting, it seems some fans are determined not to waste a single minute of GTA 6's release - no matter the cost or extra effort.
Additional reporting: Kris Bramwell
